topics.label: Aerosol science and modeling
topics.description: Follow a scientific question from particles and gases to processes, models, and research applications.
topics.context: An aerosol links a population of particles to a surrounding gas. A useful model starts with the quantity you need to explain—size, composition, lifetime, or an observable—and follows only the mechanisms needed to connect inputs to that quantity. These branches connect scientific explanations with runnable calculations and their evidence.
topics.investigation: Choose one measured change in your system. Which state variables and processes could cause it, and what diagnostic would distinguish competing explanations?

topics.label: Describe an aerosol
topics.description: Connect size, composition, population representation, and the surrounding gas to the properties you can measure.
topics.context: Before evolving an aerosol, decide what each stored quantity represents. Radius and diameter, counts and number densities, and individual mass and bulk mass can describe the same system in different ways. Establishing those meanings makes later process comparisons interpretable.
topics.investigation: Can you reconstruct total number and material mass from your initial data, including the physical volume and distribution measure?

topics.label: Understand aerosol processes
topics.description: Explore how particles form, grow, collide, and leave a system.
topics.context: Different mechanisms can produce similar-looking size changes. Condensation transfers material between gas and particles; coagulation redistributes particle material while reducing number; sources and losses change the modeled inventory. Combining them requires diagnostics that retain those distinctions.
topics.investigation: If a size-distribution peak shifts, what simultaneous measurements of gas, particle number, and mass would identify the responsible mechanism?

topics.label: Numerical modeling
topics.description: Choose numerical methods and execution paths, then assess the evidence behind a model result.
topics.context: Build on a defined aerosol population to choose timesteps, numerical precision, and an execution path. Representation choices still affect what the model resolves. Conservation, numerical convergence, physical comparison, and performance answer separate questions.
topics.investigation: Which modeling choice could change your scientific conclusion, and what controlled comparison would measure that sensitivity?

topics.label: Explore research applications
topics.description: Bring processes together around laboratory and environmental questions.
topics.context: Coupled examples show how processes interact around a research question. Their initial conditions, forcing, and material assumptions are illustrative unless an independent reference is supplied. Use them to develop a study design, then replace demonstration inputs with evidence for your own system.
topics.investigation: Which part of an example can transfer to your experiment, and which boundary conditions or material properties must be re-established?

topics.label: Size distributions
topics.description: Relate a size spectrum to particle number, bin widths, and changes of coordinates.
topics.context: A curve may represent number per bin, per unit radius, or per logarithmic interval. Its height and peak can change under conversion even when it describes the same particles. Integrated number and material provide checks when comparing instruments, model inputs, and simulation outputs.
topics.investigation: Transform a measured spectrum into your model representation. Does integrated number remain consistent after accounting for bin width and radius versus diameter?

topics.label: Composition and properties
topics.description: Explore how material composition shapes water uptake, surface behavior, and interaction with light.
topics.context: Particles of equal size can contain different materials and respond differently to humidity or light. Bulk averages do not always preserve those responses. Material ordering, mixing state, density, and the chosen thermodynamic or optical model connect stored composition to an observable.
topics.investigation: Would two populations with the same bulk composition but different particle-to-particle mixing states produce the same observable under your assumptions?

topics.label: Gas and environment
topics.description: Specify the gas mixture, temperature, and pressure that surround the particles.
topics.context: Gas concentration, temperature, and pressure establish the environment for particle evolution. A stored saturation field is not automatically an evolving humidity diagnostic; current gas concentration and the selected vapor-pressure model may need to be evaluated together. Prescribed conditions and coupled reservoirs imply different budgets.
topics.investigation: Does your calculation hold vapor or temperature fixed, or update them as particles evolve? How does that choice change the inventory you should check?

topics.label: Chemical activity
topics.description: Compare ideal mixing, hygroscopicity, and nonideal organic–water interactions.
topics.context: Chemical activity describes how a component in a mixture differs from its pure-substance reference. Ideal, κ-based, and nonideal models encode different assumptions and input requirements. Their consequences appear in equilibrium surface pressure, water uptake, and phase partitioning.
topics.investigation: At fixed dry material and humidity, how much does predicted water uptake change when the activity model changes, and which composition data support that choice?

topics.label: Surface and curvature
topics.description: Connect surface tension and particle curvature to the equilibrium vapor pressure.
topics.context: Curvature and surface tension alter the equilibrium vapor pressure at a particle surface. This creates a size dependence that can compete with composition-driven lowering of vapor pressure. A surface mixing rule is a model assumption, especially when composition changes during growth.
topics.investigation: For your radius and composition range, does changing the surface-tension model alter the predicted direction of mass transfer or an activation threshold?

topics.label: Optical properties
topics.description: Calculate sphere scattering, absorption, polarization, and population optical depth.
topics.context: Optical calculations connect size, refractive index, and wavelength to scattering and absorption. Single-sphere quantities must be weighted by the population measure to obtain bulk properties. The sphere model and material optical constants bound the interpretation of a comparison with observations.
topics.investigation: Can two populations with similar total mass produce different extinction or angular scattering? Hold material assumptions fixed and vary the size distribution to test that sensitivity.

topics.label: Vapor pressure
topics.description: Relate saturation vapor pressure and gas concentration to temperature and humidity.
topics.context: Saturation vapor pressure is a material-and-temperature property; partial pressure also depends on the actual gas abundance. Their ratio determines saturation with respect to the chosen reference. Empirical fits require their own temperature domain, pressure units, and coefficient convention.
topics.investigation: Would a predicted growth or evaporation transition persist with another justified vapor-pressure fit over their common validity range?

topics.label: Gas transport properties
topics.description: Examine viscosity and mean free path before using them in particle transport calculations.
topics.context: Viscosity and mean free path connect gas conditions to particle drag and diffusion. Slip and transport-regime corrections become important as particle size approaches relevant molecular length scales. Supplying consistent temperature and pressure across helpers avoids an internally inconsistent kernel.
topics.investigation: At fixed particle sizes, how does changing gas pressure alter the transport regime and a collision or deposition rate?

topics.label: Gas–particle exchange
topics.description: Follow material between vapor and particles, from growth rates to equilibrium composition.
topics.context: Gas–particle exchange can be studied as an instantaneous transfer rate, a time-dependent trajectory, or an equilibrium endpoint. These calculations answer different questions. Finite reservoirs couple particles through shared vapor, while prescribed vapor behaves as an external supply.
topics.investigation: Does your research require the time to approach equilibrium, or only the equilibrium state—and can the reservoir supply the required material?

topics.label: Particle collisions
topics.description: Compare collision mechanisms and the representations used to evolve a population.
topics.context: A collision kernel describes a pairwise interaction coefficient. Population abundance determines how often those interactions occur. Brownian motion, electrical forces, turbulence, and settling can change pair rates, while the population representation determines how collisions change the stored distribution.
topics.investigation: Are differences in your predicted collision loss driven by the kernel, the initial abundance, or the numerical representation? Change one at a time.

topics.label: Formation and removal
topics.description: Account for particles entering, forming within, or leaving the modeled system.
topics.context: Particle formation, injection, dilution, and wall deposition all change abundance, but they cross different inventory boundaries. Formation can consume a modeled precursor; an external injection adds material; removal carries it away. Keep those budgets explicit before coupling processes.
topics.investigation: Can the change in particle material be reconciled with gas transfer and cumulative external inputs and losses over the same interval?

topics.label: Condensation and evaporation
topics.description: Interpret mass-transfer rates, water uptake, and finite-vapor growth.
topics.context: Growth is driven by the difference between ambient vapor and the composition- and curvature-dependent surface equilibrium. Particles in a finite reservoir compete for vapor; in a maintained reservoir they draw on an external supply. Size growth, water uptake, and latent-energy transfer are related diagnostics, not interchangeable ones.
topics.investigation: At fixed initial composition, does increasing particle abundance suppress growth through vapor depletion? Compare maintained and finite reservoirs while tracking total material.

topics.label: Phase equilibrium and partitioning
topics.description: Explore how compounds distribute among gas and condensed phases.
topics.context: Equilibrium partitioning asks how material is distributed among phases under the specified thermodynamic model. It does not supply the time needed to reach that state. Activity, volatility, and possible phase separation influence the endpoint and can change how bulk composition relates to particle composition.
topics.investigation: Does a kinetic simulation approach the same partitioning endpoint under matched assumptions, and what timescale prevents that endpoint from being reached?

topics.label: Brownian coagulation
topics.description: Follow diffusion-driven collisions through binned and particle-resolved calculations.
topics.context: Diffusive collisions merge particles, reducing number while ideally retaining material. PMF, PDF, and particle-resolved methods express the population differently, so compare integrated number and mass before interpreting spectra. Similar number-decay curves alone do not establish numerical convergence or identical mixing state.
topics.investigation: How does a predicted number-loss time change under grid, sample-size, and timestep refinement when physical concentration is held fixed?

topics.label: Charged particles and ions
topics.description: Explore charge-dependent collisions, ion attachment, and charge inventories.
topics.context: Electrical interactions can alter collisions, while ion attachment and recombination evolve charge populations. A prescribed charge-versus-size curve is distinct from a coupled charging calculation. Interpret pair kernels, particle number, material inventory, and charge inventory according to the processes actually enabled.
topics.investigation: Does a charge-dependent collision effect survive comparison with neutral particles at the same sizes and abundances, and does evolving the charge change the answer?

topics.label: Cloud-droplet collision kernels
topics.description: Compare turbulence and sedimentation models with digitized DNS reference data.
topics.context: Cloud-droplet collision models describe how turbulent motion and settling influence pair encounters. Comparison with digitized DNS data requires matching the reference conditions, plotted quantity, and model assumptions. Agreement with one reference case does not establish universal applicability.
topics.investigation: Which radius pairs and flow conditions drive disagreement with a reference kernel, and can the difference be traced to assumptions rather than plotting or digitization conventions?

topics.label: Nucleation and particle sources
topics.description: Introduce new particles while tracking source rates and material inventories.
topics.context: A formation law must be connected to particle size, composition, physical volume, and gas availability before it can populate a simulation. Fixed-capacity storage also requires an explicit exhaustion policy. Material conservation checks bookkeeping; it does not validate a nucleation coefficient or its domain.
topics.investigation: At the same available precursor mass, how does assumed formation diameter change particle number and subsequent competition for vapor?

topics.label: Wall loss and dilution
topics.description: Distinguish deposition on chamber walls from losses caused by dilution.
topics.context: Dilution removes an ideal well-mixed fraction without changing individual particle size. Wall deposition can depend on size, chamber geometry, and transport. Both lower modeled inventory, so apparent particle loss should be compared with a source-and-sink budget rather than a closed-mass assertion.
topics.investigation: Can a size-independent dilution baseline explain an observed decay, or is an additional size-dependent wall-loss mechanism required?

topics.label: Population representations
topics.description: Choose binned or resolved storage and understand count, density, and volume semantics.
topics.context: Binned concentrations, densities per radius, and resolved count weights encode different population measures. Physical volume converts represented counts to number density. The representation also determines whether particle-to-particle composition differences are retained, averaged, or absent.
topics.investigation: What information would be lost by converting your population to a coarser representation, and would that information affect the observable you care about?

topics.label: Numerical methods
topics.description: Examine timesteps, stiffness, conservation, and precision before interpreting trajectories.
topics.context: A stable-looking trajectory can still have timestep or discretization error. Conservation tests detect inventory inconsistencies, whereas refinement tests assess sensitivity to resolution. Coupled-process ordering and stochastic variability need separate attention, especially near thresholds or depleted reservoirs.
topics.investigation: Does the quantity behind your conclusion converge when you refine the timestep, rather than merely keep the mass residual small?

topics.label: CPU and GPU execution
topics.description: Choose an execution path with explicit device, transfer, and lifecycle requirements.
topics.context: CPU, direct Warp, resident, and prepared execution paths differ in ownership and lifecycle. Transfers and checkpoints determine which copy of state a diagnostic observes. Device choice should preserve the scientific model while making precision, supported processes, and synchronization explicit.
topics.investigation: Are two execution paths advancing the same inputs and process sequence, and are their diagnostics taken from equivalent synchronized states?

topics.label: Verification and comparison
topics.description: Read numerical comparisons and recorded qualification evidence with their limits.
topics.context: Use several forms of evidence together: analytic limits, inventory checks, refinement, cross-implementation comparison, and external observations. Each rules out different errors. Performance measurements also need workload, device, synchronization, and accuracy context to be scientifically useful.
topics.investigation: What plausible error would remain undetected by your current checks, and which independent diagnostic would expose it?

topics.label: CPU workflows
topics.description: Construct native aerosol state and run supported processes on the CPU.
topics.context: A small native CPU calculation makes particle, gas, and environment state easy to inspect. Use it to establish units, source mappings, and process semantics before scaling the workload. An explicit reference case is also useful when comparing another execution backend.
topics.investigation: Can you explain each change after one process step using its material, number, and environmental assumptions before composing a longer simulation?

topics.label: GPU workflows
topics.description: Prepare resident simulations, manage transfers and checkpoints, or use direct kernels.
topics.context: Accelerated simulations benefit from retaining state on the device, but preparation, workspace capacity, checkpoints, and stochastic state become part of the workflow. Prepared examples expose these choices alongside scientific diagnostics. A faster run is useful only if its supported model and evidence answer the same question.
topics.investigation: For a representative workload, how much time is spent advancing physics versus transferring or inspecting state, and what numerical agreement is required?

topics.label: Custom processes and fields
topics.description: Extend a calculation with timed chemistry, particle tracers, and explicit backend behavior.
topics.context: Custom processes and fields let a model retain research-specific quantities such as tracers or timed chemistry. Their update rules must remain consistent with particle identity, merging, source insertion, and execution backend. Registration alone does not establish the physical semantics of a field.
topics.investigation: If particles merge or new particles appear, what should happen to your tracer—and which controlled example would verify that rule?

topics.label: Chamber experiments
topics.description: Connect humidity forcing, droplet growth, and wall losses in illustrative chamber studies.
topics.context: Chamber studies combine forcing, finite reservoirs, growth, collisions, and losses within a defined geometry. Repeated cycles can depend on the state left by previous cycles. Match time-dependent boundary conditions and inventory accounting before treating a simulation as an experimental analogue.
topics.investigation: After a humidity cycle, which particle properties retain memory of the previous cycle, and can that memory be separated from wall loss or changing gas supply?

topics.label: Atmospheric processes
topics.description: Follow aerosol through changing air or compare its response across prescribed environments.
topics.context: Temperature, pressure and humidity can be sampled along a parcel’s path or specified independently across a set of experiments. Following a parcel keeps track of its water and particle inventories through time. Sampling many environments reveals which combinations change an aerosol response.
topics.investigation: How does a rise through cloud base compare with separate experiments at the same temperatures and pressures, and which differences come from the aerosol’s earlier history?

topics.label: Parcels
topics.description: Track water and particles in a rising air parcel or across the faces of a parcel cluster.
topics.context: In a rising parcel, cooling and condensation change how much water remains as vapor and how much enters droplets. Replaying the same air history under prescribed humidity lets you measure the water supplied or removed by that constraint. In a cluster, tracking each face crossing shows which parcel gained or lost material and how particles moved relative to the air.
topics.investigation: When an updraft lifts a group of parcels, which particles rise above their original altitude while settling into the group below?

topics.label: Atmospheric environment sweeps
topics.description: Compare aerosol growth and charging across prescribed temperature, pressure, humidity and ion conditions.
topics.context: Separate runs expose the same initial aerosol to different gas conditions. Compare final size distributions and particle charge across dry and humid cases. Each result depends on the environmental variables varied together and the assumed ion supply.
topics.investigation: When the initial aerosol and ion supply are held fixed, how much does changing the environment alter the final size and charge distributions?

topics.label: Emissions and exposure
topics.description: Explore illustrative smoke, soot, and respiratory-droplet calculations.
topics.context: Smoke, soot, and respiratory droplets combine source properties with changing environmental conditions. Demonstration scenarios help identify competing mechanisms, but source composition and exposure interpretation require independent evidence. A particle evolution model alone does not establish a health outcome.
topics.investigation: Which source property most affects the predicted size or lifetime in your scenario, and what measurement would constrain it before interpreting downstream exposure?

topics.label: Direct kernels
topics.description: Control individual CUDA process calls and explicit transfers.
topics.context: Direct kernels expose the boundary between host state, device buffers, and individual aerosol processes. Each call needs compatible configuration and capacity; a successful launch alone does not establish physical agreement.
topics.investigation: How does a direct condensation or coagulation step compare with an independent reference at matched initial conditions?

topics.label: Prepared simulations
topics.description: Prepare a process sequence and evolve one or many aerosol boxes.
topics.context: Preparation binds state, process choices, and workspaces before repeated execution. Forcing, stochastic state, and heterogeneous boxes affect both interpretation and cost; comparisons should retain the same workload.
topics.investigation: How do forcing and the number of boxes change evolution and runtime for the same process configuration?

topics.label: Resident execution
topics.description: Continue device-resident runs, save checkpoints, and replay schedules.
topics.context: Resident workflows retain device state across timesteps. Restart and graph replay must preserve the supported state and execution contracts; reusable schedules have explicit qualification boundaries.
topics.investigation: Does a checkpoint restart reproduce uninterrupted evolution, including the stochastic state?

topics.label: GPU foundations
topics.description: Choose a supported backend and understand device ownership.
topics.context: GPU setup, data movement, and kernel implementation answer different questions. Backend availability does not imply every scientific model or execution path is supported.
topics.investigation: Which setup, data ownership, and implementation constraints determine whether a proposed GPU study is supported?

topics.label: Setup and support
topics.description: Check backend availability, supported features, and failures.
topics.context: Device selection and support tables establish which execution paths are available. Explicit fallback choices and diagnostic messages should be checked before interpreting results as CUDA evidence.
topics.investigation: Can the selected backend execute the required processes without an unintended fallback?

topics.label: Device data and capacity
topics.description: Manage transfers, slots, and finite device capacity.
topics.context: Transfers establish ownership boundaries between host and device state. Finite slot capacity can limit source and collision workflows; capacity exhaustion must remain visible rather than silently changing the population.
topics.investigation: How much capacity does a source-driven run need, and what happens when that capacity is exhausted?

topics.label: Warp implementation
topics.description: Understand data structures, kernels, and differentiation limits.
topics.context: Warp architecture and teaching material explain how particle operations map to device execution. Teaching examples and differentiation discussions do not by themselves qualify a production aerosol model.
topics.investigation: Which operations in a particle workflow are differentiable, and which stochastic or discrete choices break that interpretation?

topics.label: Scientific and numerical correctness
topics.description: Compare equations, conservation, and numerical refinement.
topics.context: Analytic limits, independent calculations, and refinement studies constrain different numerical errors. A parity result establishes agreement for its tested conditions, not universal physical validity.
topics.investigation: Do conservation and refinement checks agree with an independent reference across the intended parameter range?

topics.label: Execution and release qualification
topics.description: Inspect evidence for supported workflows and release gates.
topics.context: Qualification records tie claims to a particular implementation, workload, and device. Passing one workflow or release gate does not imply qualification of other backends or configurations.
topics.investigation: Which recorded gates cover the exact workflow and revision needed for a new study?

topics.label: Performance and memory evidence
topics.description: Interpret timings, scaling, and device memory budgets.
topics.context: Runtime and memory measurements depend on workload, synchronization, hardware, and numerical agreement. Historical benchmarks retain their provenance and should not be presented as current measurements.
topics.investigation: How does throughput change with population size when accuracy and device memory limits are held explicit?

topics.label: Constructing aerosol state
topics.description: Build particle, gas, and environment state from scientific inputs.
topics.context: Initial state encodes units, species mapping, physical volume, and population measure. Construction should preserve the intended number and material inventories before any process advances.
topics.investigation: Do the constructed state and input measurements represent the same integrated number and species mass?

topics.label: Population measures and weights
topics.description: Distinguish particle properties from population weights.
topics.context: Bin totals, densities per coordinate, and resolved count weights have different integration rules. Matching array shapes is insufficient to establish that two populations represent the same aerosol.
topics.investigation: Which integration and volume factors make two population representations comparable?

topics.label: State ownership and transfers
topics.description: Access and transfer native state without losing its meaning.
topics.context: Container access, field ownership, and transfer rules determine whether a change updates the intended state. Shape, species metadata, and population semantics must survive supported transfers.
topics.investigation: Which state values and metadata remain invariant after a supported transfer and reconstruction?

topics.label: Ideal mixtures
topics.description: Connect composition measures to ideal chemical activity.
topics.context: Ideal mixing uses a specified composition measure and pure-component reference. Equal mass fractions need not imply equal mole fractions or equal equilibrium contributions.
topics.investigation: How do ideal activities change when the same mixture is expressed in mass and mole fractions?

topics.label: Hygroscopicity and κ models
topics.description: Relate water content to a hygroscopicity approximation.
topics.context: A κ model summarizes water uptake with an effective hygroscopicity parameter. Its assumptions and composition inputs bound comparisons with more detailed activity models.
topics.investigation: How sensitive is predicted water uptake to κ at fixed dry composition?

topics.label: Nonideal mixtures
topics.description: Explore composition-dependent departures from ideal activity.
topics.context: Nonideal models introduce interactions beyond an ideal mixing rule. Comparisons require matched composition, temperature, and model applicability; departures from unity are model predictions rather than direct observations.
topics.investigation: Where does the BAT activity prediction depart most from ideal mixing along a composition path?

topics.label: Binned populations
topics.description: Follow Brownian collisions with bin totals or size densities.
topics.context: PMF and PDF populations encode different measures of the same size coordinate. Collision changes should be interpreted through integrated number and mass with the appropriate bin weights.
topics.investigation: Do PMF and PDF calculations agree after integrating both over identical size bins?

topics.label: Particle-resolved populations
topics.description: Track collisions through individual representative particles.
topics.context: Resolved collisions change particle properties and represented counts through discrete events. Random variation and count weights must be considered when comparing with a deterministic population calculation.
topics.investigation: How does ensemble particle-number decay compare with a matched binned calculation?

topics.label: Comparing representations
topics.description: Match units and inventories before comparing coagulation.
topics.context: Similar spectra or number-decay curves can hide differences in population measure or mixing state. Cross-representation comparisons need matched initial inventories and numerical refinement.
topics.investigation: Which apparent differences disappear after matching population measures, and which persist under refinement?

topics.label: Population growth and vapor reservoirs
topics.description: Compare growth in maintained and finite vapor reservoirs.
topics.context: A maintained reservoir supplies vapor externally, whereas a finite reservoir couples particles through vapor depletion. Growth and water uptake therefore require different inventory accounting.
topics.investigation: How does finite vapor availability change growth relative to a maintained reservoir?

topics.label: Adaptive growth and relaxation
topics.description: Resolve depletion and stiff wet–dry relaxation on CPU and CUDA.
topics.context: Adaptive studies examine error control when growth and equilibration timescales vary. Oscillations in a dry regime must be distinguished from resolved physical relaxation using independent references and refinement.
topics.investigation: Do tighter integration tolerances remove dry-phase oscillations while preserving the wet-phase relaxation?

topics.label: Latent-energy transfer
topics.description: Relate phase-change mass transfer to its energy diagnostic.
topics.context: Latent energy follows from transferred material and the chosen thermodynamic properties. Computing that diagnostic does not by itself imply that temperature feedback is coupled into the simulation.
topics.investigation: How does the latent-energy diagnostic change with the mass condensed during a step?

topics.label: Dilution
topics.description: Remove a well-mixed fraction without shrinking particles.
topics.context: Ideal dilution reduces population abundance while leaving individual particle size unchanged. Inventory loss belongs to an explicit sink budget rather than a closed-system conservation assertion.
topics.investigation: Does dilution reduce integrated number and mass by the same factor while preserving particle size?

topics.label: Wall deposition
topics.description: Compare geometry and size-dependent wall removal.
topics.context: Wall deposition depends on transport, particle size, and chamber geometry. A changing spectrum can combine removal with coagulation or growth, so separate process contributions are needed.
topics.investigation: How do spherical and rectangular chamber models change size-resolved loss under comparable conditions?

topics.label: Interparticle forces
topics.description: Explore how dispersion, charge and dielectric polarization change aerosol encounter rates.
topics.context: Particle geometry and surface separation set the energy landscape of an encounter. Its barrier can suppress collisions even when the energy becomes attractive close to contact.
topics.investigation: At fixed sizes, how does charging the smaller sphere change the measured and predicted rate?
